issuing_authority: Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, Government of India
target_group: Meritorious students from economically weaker families studying in Class IX in government, government-aided or local body schools

eligibility_rules.description: Regular student in a government, government-aided or local body school (Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, residential government schools and private schools are excluded)
Parental income from all sources up to Rs 3,50,000 per year
Passed the state-level MAT and SAT selection test with at least 40% in aggregate (32% for SC/ST)
At least 55% marks in the qualifying exam (5% relaxation for SC/ST)
eligibility_rules.note: Para 2.2 says Class VII; para 3.2 says Class VIII. Confirm which applies.

eligibility_rules.description: Renewal: at least 60% in Class X (5% relaxation for SC/ST) and clear promotion in the first attempt
Cannot hold another central government scholarship at the same time

benefits.duration: Classes IX to XII, maximum four years

required_documents: Not listed in the guideline. Confirm on the state notice and NSP.
application_steps: Appear in the state-conducted selection test (MAT and SAT) for Class VIII students (para 2.1). The test is held every November (para 7.0).
If selected, apply on NSP. The institution and then the state verify the application (para 4.3).
Open a bank account, preferably SBI or another public sector or scheduled bank, for DBT (para 4.2)
The amount is paid by DBT to the student's bank account (para 4.3)
deadline_note: No application deadline in the guideline. Arrears must be claimed within 12 months of the session (para 5.3).
source_document: NMMSS revised guidelines, Ministry of Education letter dated 10 March 2022, with Annexures I and II (uploaded NMMSSGuidelines.pdf)
open_items: Resolve the Class VII vs Class VIII marks conflict
Confirm 2026-27 selection test and NSP timelines
Confirm the document list on the state notice
